title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: how many acceptances one customer may hold
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product a customer may hold any number of dangerous-goods acceptances; there is no cap per customer. Each acceptance covers one UN entry on one booking. How acceptances combine on one booking is governed by the booking-mix rule, and how they combine on one sailing by the per-shipper sailing allotment.

## Quick answers
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of acceptances per customer? | No — no cap per customer applies. |
| How many UN entries does one acceptance cover? | One. |
| How many bookings does one acceptance sit on? | One. |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)
A chemical producer wishes to ship two different UN entries on the same booking. Because one acceptance covers one UN entry, the two entries cannot share one acceptance; each needs its own acceptance on that booking. Whether both acceptances can sit on that booking is a question for the booking-mix rule, not for this rule. The same producer's other acceptances on other bookings do not, by their number alone, stand in the way of a new one, since there is no cap per customer.
